extracted.subtask_description: AP-style newspaper reporting on international and national events (speeches, civil defense, trials, military matters) intended for general readers. The page reproduces multiple news items and advance highlights of speeches and official comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program jurisdiction for U.N. commemoration
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have now come to a complete accord that the program side of the commemoration must be exclusively and entirely organized and under the jurisdiction of the United Nations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrounding explanation: delegates will sit in the same chairs used at the 1945 Charter conference; some of the same flags will be on the stage. Four selected days of the six-day celebration are to be given over to speeches by UN delegates and officials, culminating on the anniversary of the Charter signing (June 26). The program is intended to be a high-profile, UN-controlled set of events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program quality and speaker selection
rubrics_metrics.description: "The program must be of the highest possible level. Speakers must be of international prestige so that what is said will resound around the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose and context: organizers hope the event will amount to a re‑dedication to the high ideals of the United Nations Charter. The criterion implies selecting internationally prominent speakers to ensure global impact and prestige for the commemoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil defense shelter recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on effective shelters: "The simplest kind of shelter is effective away from the area of blast... A cyclone shelter 'with three feet of earth cover and a filtering device to provide air and keep out the radioactive dust is very effective, practically 100 per cent so outside actual blast.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional context and examples: radioactivity/dust can be washed off if not heavily exposed; recommended shelters include underground shelters, a basement connected by a tunnel, or a backyard shelter connected to the house; the FCDA estimated a family could build a simple cyclone shelter for about $1,000; concrete-type cyclone/underground shelters and filtering devices are emphasized to reduce contamination risk.
